standard.title: Elements combine to communicate meaning
standard.description: explore ways that the elements of drama are combined to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning in drama across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explore where, why and how drama is created across cultures, times and places; they can identify features from other drama contexts and connect them to their own practice (Y3-4).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore ways that elements of drama are combined to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning in drama across cultures, times, places and other contexts.

nodes.label: Identifying how elements combine in specific drama
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and describe how specific elements of drama are combined in a drama work to communicate ideas or meaning.
nodes.minimum_width: Student identifies and describes at least two elements used together in a specific drama they have observed, and explains what they communicate.
nodes.typical_width: Students identify and discuss the use of elements (space, time, language, movement, character, relationships) in drama using Viewpoints questions ('What did you see?', 'How did actors make characters believable?', 'What was the purpose?'); they consider how cultural understandings shape meaning through element use.
wider: Students analyse drama from another culture or historical context, identifying how element combinations reflect specific cultural purposes or values
Students investigate how drama is used in their own community to maintain, continue and revitalise culture — and identify the element combinations that carry this meaning
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot identify and describe specific element combinations in a drama they observe, they cannot make the cross-cultural comparison the descriptor requires; 'across cultures' demands a precise enough analytical lens to identify what varies.

response_modes.reason: Use Viewpoints-based questioning protocols systematically before asking students to compare — 'What did you see?', 'How was X element used?' — to ensure they have the observation vocabulary for comparison.

success_criteria: Student identifies at least two elements in combination in a specific drama and describes what each communicates
Student can connect an element combination choice to a communicative intention or cultural context

nodes.label: Comparing element combinations across contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare how element combinations communicate differently across diverse cultural, historical and contextual drama examples.
nodes.minimum_width: Student compares element combinations in two drama examples from different cultural or historical contexts and identifies at least one meaningful difference.
nodes.typical_width: Students explore drama from other places and times, discussing how it might contribute to their own drama and how cultural understandings shape meaning; they explore how drama is used to share cultural knowledge in celebrations, ceremonies and rituals in different communities including Asia.
wider: Students investigate a specific drama tradition from a country or region in Asia in depth — exploring its conventions, element combinations, and how these reflect cultural values
Students investigate how drama from another cultural tradition uses elements to carry knowledge that wouldn't translate through Western dramatic conventions

response_modes.reason: Genuine cross-cultural comparison requires experiencing diverse examples — not just one 'other' culture; width here is the pedagogical goal, not a bonus.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of cultural, historical and contextual drama traditions is very broad; students who compare widely develop substantially richer analytical capacity and are better equipped to draw on diverse influences in their own drama-making.
success_criteria: Student identifies at least one meaningful difference in how elements are combined across two different cultural or historical drama contexts
Student explains how cultural understandings shape that difference
